title: First road band: Gil Evans and the Briggs-Evans band in Stockton
summary: Maxwell tries out for Gil Evans's Stockton band, which copies Casa Loma, Ellington, Lunceford and Hines arrangements.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well, it took a lot of really inventiveness to do that. And what was your first band you

started to travel with? What did you get, around California? Well, the first band I went out of town with was Gil Evans in 1933. A local friend of mine played in this great band. We all heard about the Briggs-Evans band up in Stockton. Ned Briggs was a bass player, Gil Evans was a piano player. And they all copied arrangements off from Casa Loma and Isham Jones and people like that. And they needed a trumpet player and I went up and tried out. And I almost didn't get the job because I always had trouble reading whole notes. I always wanted to play them twice as fast. But I got the job eventually.

So I stayed with them and I copied off a few arrangements for them. I copied off some Ellington arrangements, some Lunceford arrangements and an Earl Hines arrangement, I liked "Rosetta," which I insisted on singing.
: Oh, you got into that? Always had that music around the house as a kid.
